name: WF E51 reproduction check: byte-identical alcm-reference.pine
description: E50's queue item 1: is this lab's backtest process stable under re-run at all, before anything is built on any anchor? Exact byte-identical re-run of pine/alcm-reference.pine (E44's anchor), unmodified. E44 documented PF 0.34584164, DD 20.39372123%, 28 trades, long 12 (3W, -$1100.20), short 16 (1W, -$448.20).
notes: EXACT MATCH to E44's documented headline: PF 0.34584164, DD 20.39372123%, 28 trades, longNetProfit -$1100.20 (12 trades, 3W), shortNetProfit -$448.20 (16 trades, 1W) -- reproduced to the cent. This resolves E50's queue item 1 favorably: the process is NOT universally unstable. alcm-reference.pine is genuinely reproducible. This narrows E38/E47's earlier reproduction failures to something specific to those files/constructions (E47's short leg is entangled with book-occupancy timing, per HARD LESSON 24) rather than a global engine or data-revision problem -- though the root cause of THOSE two specific failures is still not isolated. name: WF E53: pine/e50b-alcm-long-only-uncoiled.pine, first run
description: Queue item 1 carried forward from E51/E52: run e50b (short leg mechanically deleted AND coilPrev removed from goLong -- the genuinely uncoiled, single-leg construction E46/E47 described in prose but never actually built) against e50a (short leg deleted, coilPrev still present), to test whether coilPrev binds on the long leg alone.
notes: NOT a fresh number -- it is BIT-FOR-BIT IDENTICAL to E47's ORIGINAL documented headline (PF 1.21869905, DD 17.44898097%, 21 trades, all long, 42.86% win, dated 2026-09-02), even though pine/e47-alcm-long-cap12960.pine -- E47's own saved file, still containing coilPrev and the full intact short leg -- does NOT reproduce that number when re-run today (wf-e50-e47-reproduction-check: PF 0.58008733, 24 trades, 9 long/15 short). get_trades on this result (free read, no credit spent) confirms all 21 rows direction=long, matching E47's per-trade description exactly. The most parsimonious explanation: the code that actually generated E47's original number was equivalent to e50b's construction (uncoiled, short leg genuinely absent) -- not to what is currently saved under the e47 filename. That file appears to have drifted from, or was never actually, the source of its own headline -- a new variant of HARD LESSON 21 (saved source that does not match its own result), not the engine non-determinism E50 left open as the leading hypothesis. Against e50a (coiled, PF 0.45694023, 10 trades): meaningfully more trades (21 vs 10) and a different PF, so per the pre-registered outcomes in e50b's own header, coilPrev DOES bind on the long leg alone, consistent with E45's finding that the coil is a liability on this leg. This is the first PF > 1.0 result in the ALCM family since the reproducibility crisis began (E44 HARD LESSON 25) at 21 trades, right at the ~20-trade floor -- read cautiously, and not yet trusted without a same-cycle cold re-run (see wf-e54).

name: WF E63a 5m rescale H1
description: The timeframe rescale. e58a (shield $1,000, the family's largest sample at 36 trades and confirmed reproducible by E59's cold re-run) moved from a 1m to a 5m entry. 15m was rejected in design: the 15m level is reconstructed from timestamps, so on a 15m entry each bar IS one bucket, p15l collapses to the previous bar's low and brokeBelow stops being a structural level. Scaling: maxBars 6480->1296 and ta.atr(30)->atr(6), both preserving wall clock. skipOpen/skipClose are minutes, greenBull counts 1h candles, shield/rr/velK are dollars or ratios - all unscaled. notes: BOTH HALVES FAIL. E63a PF 0.70674847 / DD 31.81350346% / 95 trades / 29.47% win. E63b PF 0.83434289 / DD 16.01925213% / 73 trades / 32.88% win. That is the third of three outcomes registered before the runs. THE CEILING IS GONE AND THE EDGE WENT WITH IT: 168 trades across the two halves against the 20-30 this family had been capped at since E35, and neither half clears 1.0. THE SHARPER POINT IS IN THE BAR COUNTS: avgBarsInTrade is 225.71 and 292.85 against a 1296 cap - 17% and 23%. THE CAP DOES NOT BIND AT 5m. Every previous ALCM measurement had winners pinned at 56-93% of their cap, which is the entire reason E47 existed. So this is the FIRST measurement in this lab's history where the exit actually resolves at target or shield as the specification requires - and it returns 0.71 and 0.83. ON WHICH READING IS RIGHT: 'the ALCM family is 1m-specific' is one explanation. The simpler one is that e58a's 1.24 on 36 trades was SMALL-SAMPLE NOISE and 168 trades is the more trustworthy number. This lab's own docs have warned for weeks that 20-30 trades cannot support a ratio; this is what it looks like when that warning is finally tested. name: WF E64a: the SHORT leg under the source's own 6h direction rule
description: USER DIRECTIVE 2026-09-03: War Formation must work in both directions and the 6H is the direction. Implements ORACLE-RULES L204-216 literally -- direction = 2+ consecutive RED 6h candles, replacing the lab's own '4+ green 1h candles in the prior 6h block' proxy. Short mechanics are the structural mirror of the long's sweep-and-reclaim (15m higher high, then rejection back below). Shield $1,000 and cap 6480 held at e58a exactly so only the direction rule and the leg change.
notes: Short construction #12, and the FIRST driven by the source's own direction rule rather than by a location this lab chose. PF 0.454 on 43 trades, 6.98% win rate. THE DIRECTION RULE BINDS AND IS NOT THE PROBLEM: 43 short entries against the long leg's 28 under the identical rule (E64b), so 'red 6h' is a live, frequently-satisfied condition, not an inert gate. THE DECOMPOSITION IS THE POINT -- E64b holds the direction rule constant and runs the LONG leg at 0.959, so the leg penalty (0.959 -> 0.454) is real and separate from the direction-rule penalty (e58a's 1.240 -> E64b's 0.959). Fourteen prior mirrored shorts failed and this makes fifteen, but for the first time the failure is isolated to the MECHANICS rather than confounded with the direction. WINDOW CAVEAT, stated not excused: 4.5 months of 1m data is ONE regime, and a short leg tested only inside it cannot be distinguished from a short leg tested in a bull market. || TRADE-LEVEL FORENSICS 2026-09-04 (get_trades on jobId 01M1KM717WQKYA8668ET1KVTG0, free, no credit): THIS RESULT MEASURED THE HARNESS, NOT THE STRATEGY, AND THE EARLIER CONCLUSION DRAWN FROM IT WAS WRONG. cascadeRatio is 1 and every one of the 43 rows is a distinct entry, so unlike the 3M short there is no sliver artifact and the 6.98% win rate is arithmetically real. But the EXIT PRICES show what produced it. THE THREE WINNERS ALL EXIT AT EXACTLY 2000.0 POINTS OF PROFIT (91938.7->89938.7, 89266.2->87266.2, 81226.4->79226.4) -- the fixed dollar target, working exactly as the ALCM specifies. THE FORTY LOSERS EXIT AT WILDLY INCONSISTENT AND ABSURDLY SMALL ADVERSE DISTANCES: +0.013% (63173.8-> 63182.0), +0.017% (67927.6->67939.0), +0.035%, +0.046%, +0.071%, ranging up to +0.585%. A SHIELD IS A FIXED DOLLAR GAP AND WOULD PRODUCE A CONSISTENT LOSS DISTANCE. THESE ARE NOT SHIELD EXITS. They are margin liquidations firing wherever the engine's margin check happens to trip, and the observed 0.013% to 0.585% band brackets the ~0.35% ceiling of HARD LESSON 34 exactly. THE STRATEGY'S OWN EXIT NEVER GETS TO RUN. WHY IT HITS SHORTS AND NOT LONGS, which is the part that was not understood before: for a SHORT, an adverse move raises the loss AND raises the notional, so required margin rises while equity falls and at 100% of equity with margin_short=100 the two cross almost immediately. For a LONG, an adverse move SHRINKS the notional, so required margin falls alongside equity and they never cross. The asymmetry is a property of the margin formula, not a bug and not a strategy defect. WHAT THIS OVERTURNS: the standing conclusion that 'the short's problem is the mechanics, not the direction' is WRONG, and so is the queue item built on it, which reasoned that a 4-7% win rate is 'a statement about WHERE and WHEN the short enters'. It is a statement about POSITION SIZE. The achieved win/loss ratio here is about 6:1 (avg winner ~$217 against avg loser ~$35.80), whose break-even win rate is 14.2% -- so the geometry is not even bad, it simply never gets a fair trial. E64a, E66 and E67 differ from each other by noise on top of a harness artifact, and NO ENTRY-GEOMETRY CHANGE CAN FIX ANY OF THEM. THE ONLY WAY TO TEST THE SHORT LEG is to cut position size (roughly 25-50% of equity) so the margin boundary sits outside the shield. That is a DECLARED DEVIATION from the forced parity profile and must be labelled as one on every run that uses it, never applied silently, and never compared to a 100%-equity long without saying so.

name: WF E64b: the LONG leg under the same 6h direction rule -- the CONTROL
description: The control that makes E64a interpretable (HARD LESSON 10). Holds the LEG at e58a's long and changes ONLY the direction source: 2+ consecutive GREEN 6h candles instead of 4+ green 1h candles inside the prior 6h block. Shield, cap, velK, whole-number band, time gate and witching ban all held at e58a.
notes: NOT KEPT -- RATCHET v2 clause 1 fails outright: PF 1.24015239 (e58a) -> 0.95884068, and the count drops 36 -> 28. AND THIS IS THE UNCOMFORTABLE FINDING OF THE CYCLE: the source's OWN literal direction rule performs WORSE than the proxy this lab invented to stand in for it. ORACLE-RULES L215-216 has been asserting for some time that the straight 6h-candle count is 'simpler and better specified' than the 4-green-1h proxy. Measured, it is simpler and WORSE on this window. The proxy was doing real work -- most likely because '4 of the last ~6 1h candles green' is a persistence condition, while '2 consecutive 6h candles green' can be satisfied by two barely-green blocks. Reported plainly rather than buried: mastering the user's strategy means measuring its stated rules, INCLUDING when the measurement is inconvenient. The source rule is NOT adopted and it is NOT discarded on one 4.5-month window; e58a's proxy remains the reference build.

name: WF E66: short leg on e58a's PROXY direction rule (4+ red 1h in prior 6h), not raw 6h colour
description: Queue item 1 (STRATEGY-LEDGER.md HARD LESSON 32 item 2; EXPERIMENT-LOG.md's renumbered E66). E64 showed the source's own literal '2+ consecutive red/green 6h candle' direction rule (E64b long control PF 0.95884068) underperforms e58a's own 4-green-1h-in-prior-6h-block PERSISTENCE proxy (PF 1.24015239), and that E64a's mirrored short on the raw-6h rule scored only PF 0.45442725 (43 trades). This build isolates the short leg against the direction rule that demonstrably works instead of the one just shown to underperform: bearRegime = 4+ RED 1h candles inside the PRIOR completed 6h block (redPrev>=4, cntPrev>=5), the exact structural mirror of e58a's bullRegime/greenBull. Mechanics otherwise identical to E64a's short (brokeAbove: 15m sweep to a higher high, then a rejection crossunder back below it -- the same 'let the enemy finish' location solve the long gets for free, per ORACLE-RULES L175-177 / HARD LESSON 31 scoping of LESSON 6). shieldUsd=$1000, maxBars=6480, rr=2.0 held exactly at e58a's values (HARD LESSON 28/29: shield and hold cap are coupled, named in advance). Saved to pine/e66-proxy-direction-short.pine before running.
notes: REJECTED under RATCHET v2 clause 1, and decisively -- this is the WORST short construction result on record in this lab, below E64a's raw-6h-colour short (0.454) and below every prior mirrored short (E9/E9b/E13/E25-29). The pre-registered branch that landed: 'PF at or below E64a's 0.454 -> the proxy fix that helped the long does nothing for the short; the location solve itself needs revisiting, not the direction source feeding it.' Trade count nearly doubled versus E64a (66 vs 43) and win rate nearly halved (4.55% vs 6.98%, 3W/63L) -- the PERSISTENCE proxy that tightened the long's regime (cutting E64b's 28 down toward e58a's disciplined 36 via a stricter bar-by-bar count) does the OPPOSITE on the short side: redPrev>=4 out of a >=5-block window is evidently a much LOOSER bar than '2 consecutive fully-red 6h candles', admitting far more marginal bear regimes rather than fewer. get_trades (jobId 01M1N81TJV383JMJ2TQJBS3M1Y) confirms a genuinely different trade population from every sibling: first entry 1765955400000, matching neither e58a's long (1766151300000) nor a degenerate count -- the occupancy point named in advance (LESSON 24/28) held. avgBarsLosing 118.7 vs avgBarsWinning 1251.7: losses hit the shield fast and consistently (63 of 66), the 3 wins are large reversals the geometry stumbles into rather than selects for. THE FINDING: on this construction and window, the proxy-vs-raw-6h direction choice does NOT generalize symmetrically across legs -- it helped the long (0.959->1.240) and hurt the short even more than the raw rule already had (0.454->0.300). The short leg's defect is the MECHANICS (brokeAbove+rejection sweep, or the redPrev persistence count itself measured on RED bars specifically), not which direction-rule flavor feeds it. Fourteenth-plus mirrored/source-faithful short construction to fail in this project; per HARD LESSON 31 this remains evidence about constructions tried, not evidence the short side cannot exist -- e58a's proxy long (PF 1.240, unchanged) remains the reference build either way.

name: WF E67: E66 short + 3m cycle-position gate restored (cyclePos>=0.7, E13's own value)
description: Queue item 1 this cycle: 'stop varying the direction rule and attack the short's entry geometry.' Three source-faithful shorts had failed under the ALCM exit (E64a 0.454/43, E66 0.300/66, a v34-era build below 1.0), all with catastrophic win rates (4-7%) against an rr of 2.0 that needs 33% -- a signature of the stop being hit almost every time, i.e. a statement about WHERE/WHEN the short enters. The ONE hypothesis: E64a and E66 both entered on brokeAbove (genuine 15m-high sweep) + rejection crossunder with NO check on where price sits inside its recent range -- exactly the failure ORACLE-RULES names ('do you want to short down here?', entering after price has already fallen). This project has ONE proven fix for that failure: the 3-minute cycle-position gate (cyclePos = rolling 30-min close-to-range position, shorts only when cyclePos>=0.7, i.e. still near the top of the recent swing), the ONLY term in this lab's entire short-construction history that ever improved a short leg (E13: PF 0.68->0.75), and ORACLE-RULES explicitly says 'keep the gate in all future short builds.' E64a and E66 both omitted it. This run is the single-variable change: E66 + shortCycleGate, everything else (proxy direction rule, brokeAbove+rejection geometry, shieldUsd=$1000, maxBars=6480, rr=2.0, velK=0.8, inMiddle) held exactly at E66's values. cycleWinMins/cycleHiThresh set to E13's own values (30 minutes, 0.7), not re-tuned. Saved to pine/e67-e66-cyclegate.pine before running.
notes: REJECTED under RATCHET v2 (trade count 12, well below the ~20 interpretability floor and the 30-trade KEEP floor; PF 0.00, 0 wins / 12 losses). The hypothesis is FALSIFIED, decisively: restoring the one term this project has ever shown to help a short leg did not help this construction -- it drove the win rate from E66's already-poor 4.55% (3W/63L) to literally zero (0W/12L), while cutting trades 66->12. This lands in the pre-registered 'trades collapse' branch, worse than anticipated (zero wins, not just a small sample). get_trades (jobId 01M1NBGP62HWSRNKC4N3DZ6S8P) shows every one of the 12 losses closed well short of the full $1,000 shield in price terms (largest single loss $72.27 gross; a full-shield loss at the recorded position sizes would run roughly $100-140) -- none hit the stop at its full width and none reached maxBars (barsInTrade ranged 2-1951 against a 6480 cap). WHAT THIS ESTABLISHES: the cycle-position gate's benefit in E13 was specific to that construction's OTHER terms (the 3m coil atrFast<atrSlow*coilK, the HA-down confirmation on the trigger candle, the tighter structural stop clamped to 0.15-1.50% of price) and does NOT transfer to this shield-based geometry in isolation -- necessary in E13's context, not a general fix. Combined with the proxy direction rule's already-tighter regime (E66's 66 vs E64a's 43), stacking the cycle gate on top over-restricts the sample past the point of being readable, and what little survives is no better than the trades it removed. QUEUE: the short's defect is still located in mechanics, not direction source (per HARD LESSON 32/E66), but the specific fix that worked once under the old exit model does not generalize alone under the ALCM shield -- a future cycle should test the OTHER entry terms named in the mandate (brokeBelow analogue, h1Bull analogue, timeGate) one at a time on the LONG side (e58a, still the reference build, untouched by this leg-only run), or reconsider the short's location solve as a combined package (coil + HA-confirmation + cycle position together, as E13 ran it) rather than the cycle gate alone -- not attempted this cycle, budget reserved after one decisive backtest (1 of 2 available spent; the result is unambiguous under the pre-registered outcomes and a second run would not change the reading).

name: WF E68: the shield is INERT on shorts -- the 5x diagnostic
description: DIAGNOSTIC, NOT A BUILD. E64a unchanged except the shield multiplied 5x, $1,000 -> $5,000, with rr held at 2.0 so the target scales with it. Run to test a suspicion raised by free get_trades analysis: that the A.L.C.M. shield never fires on a short position under the engine's forced parity profile, and that every short result this lab has produced measured the engine's margin behaviour rather than the user's strategy.
verdict: DIAGNOSTIC -- CONFIRMS THE SHIELD IS INERT ON SHORTS
notes: NUMBERING: run locally as E67 and renumbered to E68 on merge -- the cloud routine independently claimed E67 the same hour for a cycle-position-gate short (PF 0.00 on 12 trades, 0 winners). THAT RESULT IS FURTHER EVIDENCE FOR THIS ONE: twelve shorts and not a single winner is exactly what a leg whose adverse side is truncated by liquidation looks like. THE PRE-REGISTERED OUTCOME 'LOSERS UNCHANGED' IS WHAT HAPPENED. Multiplying the shield 5x moved the average loser from -$35.80 (E64a) to -$33.43, and the largest loss from -$72.80 to -$76.46. A five-fold wider stop produced statistically identical losses. THE SHIELD IS INERT ON THE SHORT SIDE. The supporting evidence came free from get_trades and is stronger than the aggregate: on e58a (LONG) every one of 36 trades exits at EXACTLY -$1,000 or +$2,000 of price, and the loss is SMALLER than the trade's max adverse excursion (seq 1 lost $113 against a `drawdown` of $138.99) -- the stop fired before the worst point, correctly. On E64a (SHORT) not one loser reaches +$1,000, the adverse exits run +$8.20 to +$503.10 in a smooth continuous distribution, and for EVERY losing short `grossProfit` equals `drawdown` to the cent. Exiting at precisely the max adverse excursion is the signature of a FORCED CLOSE, not a stop. THE MECHANISM: the engine forces percent_of_equity 100 and margin_short 100, so a short has zero excess margin AND its notional grows as price rises against it while equity falls -- the position is closed almost immediately. THE ARITHMETIC THAT CLOSES THE QUESTION: liquidation lands at roughly -$33 on $10,000, about 0.33% of equity and 0.33% of price. LESSON 3's commission floor requires a stop of at least 0.8%. SO NO VALID SHORT STOP CAN EVER FIRE BEFORE LIQUIDATION ON THIS ENGINE AT THIS SIZING -- there is no shield width that is both wide enough to clear the R floor and tight enough to bind. DO NOT READ THE 1.03088936 AS AN IMPROVEMENT. It is 2 winners in 44 trades (4.55% win rate), and both are outsized only because the target moved to $10,000; avgBarsWinning is 6,442 and one winner hit the maxBars cap. The Pine header registered in advance that winners carry no signal in this test and that only the losers do. WHAT THIS INVALIDATES: all fifteen short constructions in this lab -- E9, E9b, E13, E25, E26, E27, E64a, E66 and the rest -- were never testing the A.L.C.M. exit model. Their 4-7% win rates are an artefact of the harness, not a fact about BTC. The user's both-directions requirement CANNOT be tested for War Formation under this parity profile, and that is the honest state of the lab. WHAT IT DOES NOT INVALIDATE: every LONG result stands untouched -- e58a, e50a/e50b, alcm-reference and the rest all exit exactly on the shield, verified trade by trade. CROSS-LAB HYPOTHESIS, NOT YET A CONCLUSION: 3M's shorts (v53 0.705, v55 0.722) and the BTC lab's short attempts use STRUCTURAL stops rather than a dollar shield, so the same arithmetic may or may not apply -- their stop distances must be measured against the ~0.33% liquidation threshold before any of those results is trusted. That check is free via get_trades and is the next thing to do in both labs.

name: WF E69a: binding test -- h1Bull removed. The source calls it a bonus; it is load-bearing.
description: Queue item 2, run INSTEAD of the stored prompt's queue item 1 because the docs override it: E68 established the short leg is untestable on this engine, so another short geometry would be uninterpretable. Binding test on the long side. e58a with h1Bull (current close above the current 1h open) removed from goLong, nothing else changed. Chosen first because the SOURCE ITSELF calls this term optional -- ORACLE-RULES L211, 'Singularity = 6h and 1h the same colour. A bonus, not a requirement' -- and because bullRegime (4+ green 1h in the prior 6h block) is a prime E14 redundancy suspect saying the same thing.
notes: The third of four pre-registered outcomes landed: COUNT RISES AND PF COLLAPSES, so the term BINDS and earns its place. Removing h1Bull nearly doubles the sample (36 -> 67) and destroys the edge (PF 1.24015239 -> 0.96688238), with drawdown worsening 9.82519609% -> 14.79601157%. REJECTED under RATCHET v2 clause 1. AND IT CONTRADICTS THE SOURCE, WHICH IS THE POINT WORTH RECORDING: ORACLE-RULES L211 relays the author calling 1h agreement 'a bonus, not a requirement'. Measured, it is the single most load-bearing entry term this lab has tested -- the ONLY one whose removal takes the build from profitable to unprofitable. It is not redundant with bullRegime either, despite both meaning 'price is rising': bullRegime reads the PRIOR COMPLETED 6h block (a persistence condition on history) while h1Bull reads the CURRENT 1h candle (a liveness condition on now). One says the regime was bullish; the other says it still is. THIS IS THE SECOND TIME THE SOURCE'S OWN WEIGHTING HAS INVERTED UNDER MEASUREMENT. E64b found the source's literal 6h direction rule (0.95884068) loses to the lab's 1h-based proxy (1.24015239). E69a finds the 1h term the source calls optional is indispensable. Both point the same way: THE 1-HOUR TIMEFRAME CARRIES MORE OF THIS STRATEGY'S EDGE THAN THE SOURCE'S FRAMING SUGGESTS, even though the source names the 6h 'the God of direction'. That is a finding about the user's strategy, produced by measuring it faithfully rather than by redesigning it. OCCUPANCY (LESSONS 24/28/29) named in advance: removing an entry filter admits more trades and shifts every downstream admission, so this is NOT a controlled superset of e58a's 36 -- firstTradeEntryTs 1766007600000 against e58a's 1766151300000 confirms trade 1 itself differs.

name: WF E69b: binding test -- the whole-number band removed. A near-miss that questions the ratchet.
description: Sibling of E69a, run together per LESSON 16. e58a with the inMiddle whole-number band (ban entries sitting 400-600 into a thousand) removed from goLong, nothing else changed. A pure filter that removes setups and never creates one, never binding-tested in this lab's history.
verdict: NOT KEPT -- fails RATCHET v2 clause 1 by 0.0103, and that is worth flagging
notes: NOT KEPT, and the rule is honoured rather than bent -- but this is the closest thing to a genuine tension the ratchet has produced. Against e58a (PF 1.24015239 / DD 9.82519609% / 36 trades): profit factor 1.22985003 is LOWER by 0.0103, which fails clause 1 outright. Everything else moved the right way. Drawdown IMPROVED 9.82519609% -> 9.28471029% (0.54pp better). Trade count rose 36 -> 43, +19% on a lab whose binding constraint is the 30-trade floor. Net return rose +7.47495942% -> +8.92191315%. Sharpe is 1.22326152. And the build has ONE FEWER TERM, so there is less surface to curve-fit. A change that improves drawdown, sample, net return and simplicity is rejected on a profit-factor difference of 0.0103 -- roughly 0.8% -- measured across two samples of 36 and 43 trades, which is far inside the noise those counts can support. THE TERM'S BINDING VERDICT: inMiddle BINDS but does not EARN ITS PLACE. It removes 7 of 43 setups (16%) and buys 0.0103 of profit factor at the cost of half a point of drawdown and 19% of the sample. THIS IS A RULE QUESTION FOR THE USER, NOT A DECISION FOR THIS LAB TO MAKE UNILATERALLY: should RATCHET v2 clause 1 admit a strict-equality band -- for instance, keep a change whose PF is within ~0.02 when drawdown improves AND the trade count rises? The existing clause 2 already contains the mirror of that idea (drawdown may worsen 0.50pp when PF improves by more than 0.02). There is no symmetric allowance in the other direction, and E69b is the first result to sit exactly in that gap. Raised, not acted on. OCCUPANCY named in advance; firstTradeEntryTs 1766151300000 matches e58a's trade 1 exactly, so unlike E69a this build shares its first entry with the parent and diverges only later.

name: WF E70a: binding test -- brokeBelow removed. The source's central claim, measured.
description: Queue item 2, run INSTEAD of the stored prompt's queue item 1 because the docs override it: E68 established the short leg is untestable on this engine (force-closed at ~0.35% adverse, below the 0.8% commission floor), so another short geometry would be uninterpretable. Parent e58a (PF 1.24015239 / DD 9.82519609% / 36 trades), confirmed reproducible E58=E59. One term removed from goLong, everything else held byte-identical. THE TERM: brokeBelow requires the current 15m bucket to sweep to a LOWER LOW than the previous bucket before the reclaim trigger can fire. It is the mechanical form of the source's central teaching -- ORACLE-RULES: 'We must let the Red Army finish', wait through the red sequence until the sellers exhaust themselves BELOW a prior level, then enter as price turns up. So this is not a parameter test, it is a test of the strategy's premise. The reclaim crossover above p15l remains; only the requirement that the bucket dipped under it first is removed.
verdict: REJECTED -- brokeBelow BINDS. The source's premise holds.
notes: REJECTED under RATCHET v2 clause 1. Removing brokeBelow takes PF 1.24015239 -> 1.03608397 and drawdown 9.82519609% -> 11.90079453%, while the count rises 36 -> 59 (+64%). SO THE SOURCE'S CENTRAL TEACHING IS DOING REAL WORK: 'let the Red Army finish' is not decoration, and the 23 extra entries admitted without it are on net materially worse. THAT IS A GENUINE VINDICATION OF THE USER'S STRATEGY and it deserves saying as plainly as the inversions do. BUT NOTE THE RANK. Removing brokeBelow leaves the build ABOVE 1.0 (1.036); removing h1Bull did not (0.967, E69a). So the source's own central location term is LESS load-bearing than a term the source explicitly calls optional. Cascade ratio 1, so 59 is a true position count (HARD LESSON 35). Occupancy named in advance: removing an entry filter admits more trades and shifts every downstream admission, so this is not a controlled superset of e58a's 36.

name: WF E70b: binding test -- the 6h-block time gate removed. The last untested term.
description: Queue item 2, run INSTEAD of the stored prompt's queue item 1 because the docs override it: E68 established the short leg is untestable on this engine (force-closed at ~0.35% adverse, below the 0.8% commission floor), so another short geometry would be uninterpretable. Parent e58a (PF 1.24015239 / DD 9.82519609% / 36 trades), confirmed reproducible E58=E59. One term removed from goLong, everything else held byte-identical. THE TERM: timeGate bans entries in the first 60 and last 60 minutes of each 6h block, keeping only the middle four hours. It is this lab's OWN mechanisation of avoiding a higher-timeframe candle's noisy open and close -- it appears nowhere in the source material -- and it had never been measured. Sibling of E70a, run together per LESSON 16. With this pair, every entry condition in the build has a binding measurement against it.
verdict: REJECTED -- timeGate BINDS HARDER THAN THE SOURCE'S OWN LOCATION TERM
notes: REJECTED under RATCHET v2 clause 1. Removing the time gate takes PF 1.24015239 -> 1.00914071 and drawdown 9.82519609% -> 13.48685394% (the worst drawdown of the whole sweep), on 36 -> 47 trades. AND THIS IS THE UNCOMFORTABLE PART: a time-of-day filter that appears NOWHERE in the user's source material binds HARDER than brokeBelow (1.036), which is the mechanical form of the source's central teaching. The lab invented this rule; measured, it is the second most load-bearing entry term in the build. Cascade ratio 1, so 47 is a true position count. Occupancy named in advance.

name: E71: the War Formation SHORT at 25% of equity -- DECLARED DEVIATION
description: E64a byte-identical EXCEPT position size cut to 25% of equity via an explicit Pine qty, because the parity profile overrides default_qty_value. A DECLARED DEVIATION from the forced parity profile, made necessary by HARD LESSON 42: at 100% equity the engine's margin call fires long before the A.L.C.M. shield does, so all three prior shorts measured the harness rather than the strategy. Serves the user's 2026-09-03 directive that War Formation must work in both directions, with the 6H candle as the direction and red meaning shorts -- this build uses the source's LITERAL rule (2+ consecutive red 6h) rather than the lab's proxy.
verdict: THE FIRST HONEST MEASUREMENT OF THE WAR FORMATION SHORT. Not a candidate (PF under 1.0), but real.
notes: THE SHIELD BOUND ON EVERY SINGLE TRADE, VERIFIED FREE VIA get_trades AND THIS WAS THE REGISTERED FIRST READ. All 21 losers exit at EXACTLY +1000.0 points (85959.7->86959.7, 85215.7->86215.7, 90390->91390, 63173.8->64173.8, and so on without exception) and all 12 winners at EXACTLY -2000.0 points. ZERO LIQUIDATIONS, cascadeRatio 1, 33 clean entries. Compare E64a, where the same geometry at 100% equity produced losers at 0.013%, 0.017%, 0.035% ... 0.585% adverse. THE A.L.C.M. EXIT NOW WORKS EXACTLY AS THE SOURCE SPECIFIES. WHAT CHANGED, FROM A PURE SIZING CHANGE AND NOTHING ELSE: profit factor 0.45442725 -> 0.97315988, win rate 6.98% -> 36.36363636%, drawdown down to 2.66826642%. A FIVEFOLD WIN-RATE INCREASE WITH BYTE-IDENTICAL ENTRY LOGIC. This retires E64a, E66 and E67 as harness measurements and confirms HARD LESSON 42 conclusively. AND 36.36% CLEARS ITS OWN BAR: an rr of 2.0 needs 33.3%, so the short's win rate is ABOVE what its own target requires -- the thing every prior short number said was impossible. COST DECOMPOSITION: gross = net + commission = -$20.43 + $81.43 = +$61.00. THE SHORT IS GROSS-POSITIVE AND LOSES ONLY TO FEES. WHY THE RATIO IS 1.70 AND NOT 2.0 despite every exit being exactly at 1000 or 2000 POINTS: qty varies with equity and price across the window, and commission is subtracted from both sides, so the DOLLAR ratio compresses even though the POINT ratio is exactly 2.0 by construction. That is an artifact of reporting, not of the strategy. WHAT THIS IS NOT: PF 0.97315988 is under 1.0 so it is NOT a candidate and does NOT become one, and 33 trades sits at the very floor of quotability (LESSON 12). The 1m window is 4.5 months of ONE regime and CANNOT support a split -- that limit is stated, not engineered around. AND IT IS NOT COMPARABLE TO e58a's 1.24015239: that is a 100%-equity long and this is a 25%-equity short. They must never be quoted side by side as though run alike. Trade count fell 43 -> 33 exactly as the occupancy note predicted in advance, because the shield rather than a margin call now ends trades and holds lengthened enormously (avgBarsInTrade 948), so with pyramiding=1 longer holds block later entries. The drop is occupancy, NOT selectivity.

name: E72: the LONG leg at 25% of equity -- the comparability control
description: e58a byte-identical EXCEPT the same 25%-of-equity declared deviation used by E71. THE CONTROL that makes the two legs comparable. E71 measured the short honestly for the first time, but it could not be set beside any existing long number because every long in this lab was run at 100% of equity -- comparing a 25% short to a 100% long is exactly the error HARD LESSON 43 warns about. REGISTERED PREDICTION: for a LONG an adverse move SHRINKS the notional, so required margin falls alongside equity and the two never cross; a long should therefore be INSENSITIVE to the size change because its shield already bound at 100%.
verdict: PREDICTION CONFIRMED -- and this is the first TRUE BIDIRECTIONAL measurement this lab has ever had
notes: THE REGISTERED PREDICTION WAS CONFIRMED ALMOST EXACTLY, AND THE STRONGEST EVIDENCE IS NOT THE PROFIT FACTOR. Against e58a at 100% equity (PF 1.24015239 / DD 9.82519609% / 36 trades / 41.67% win): TRADE COUNT IS IDENTICAL AT 36 AND THE WIN RATE IS IDENTICAL AT 41.66666667% (15W/21L in both). An identical count AND an identical win/loss split means the size change admitted the SAME TRADE POPULATION and resolved every one of them the SAME WAY. The long was never being liquidated -- its shield already bound at 100%, exactly as the margin arithmetic predicts, because for a long an adverse move SHRINKS the notional so required margin falls alongside equity and the two never cross. Profit factor moved only 1.24015239 -> 1.26239697 (+0.022, from the changed commission-to-move ratio at smaller size), and drawdown scaled down 9.82519609% -> 2.50912733% as a smaller position mechanically should. Sharpe 1.07298256. Cascade ratio 1 on 36 clean entries. SO THE ASYMMETRY IS NOW CONFIRMED FROM BOTH SIDES: shorts were destroyed by the margin boundary (E64a 0.45442725 -> E71 0.97315988 from sizing alone, a fivefold win-rate change) while longs are untouched by the same change. HARD LESSON 42's account is complete rather than half-tested, and the expensive alternative outcome -- that longs were affected too and every 100%-equity number in this lab needed re-running -- is ruled out. THE TWO LEGS ARE NOW DIRECTLY COMPARABLE ON EQUAL TERMS FOR THE FIRST TIME IN THIS LAB'S HISTORY: LONG 1.26239697 on 36 trades at 41.67% win, SHORT 0.97315988 on 33 trades at 36.36% win, both at 25% of equity, same window, same shield, same rr. THAT IS THE ANSWER TO THE USER'S BIDIRECTIONAL DIRECTIVE, and it is a real answer rather than a harness artifact: the long works, the short is marginal but genuine -- gross-positive at +$61.00 and losing only to fees. NO CHAMPION IS DECLARED. 36 and 33 trades sit at the floor of quotability (LESSON 12) and the 1m window is 4.5 months of ONE regime that CANNOT support a split; that limit is stated, not engineered around. A SECONDARY RESULT WORTH KEEPING: e58a now reproduces its behaviour at a second position size with an identical trade population, which is a stronger reproducibility signal than a repeat run at the same settings (LESSON 25).

name: E73: short with the shield 1000->2000 and cap 6480->12960, at 25% equity
description: E71 with the shield doubled and the hold cap doubled with it, the lab's own documented linear coupling (e58a's header records maxBars 6480 as 'scaled linearly from E47's 12960 at $2,000'). Attacks the ONE constraint E71 identified: the short is GROSS-POSITIVE at +$61.00 but pays $81.43 in commission, so it loses only to fees. Commission is ~0.05% of notional per side regardless of the shield, so doubling the shield should roughly double the dollars per trade while the fee per trade stays flat. The shield axis was recorded CLOSED on the LONG at 100% equity (E57); this is the SHORT at 25%, where the binding constraint is demonstrably different.
verdict: REJECTED. 23 trades is a DIRECTION not a result -- but the GROSS SIGN FLIP is robust to that, and it closes the shield axis on the short too.
notes: FIRST, THE SAMPLE: 23 trades is BELOW the 30-trade floor, so the profit factor is a DIRECTION and NOT a result, and it is not quoted as one (LESSON 12). E71's 33 was already at the floor and the occupancy note in the Pine header predicted this drop IN ADVANCE -- holds went from 948 to 3421 average bars, a 3.6x increase, and with pyramiding=1 longer holds block later entries. The count fall is OCCUPANCY, not selectivity. THE GROSS SIGN FLIP IS ROBUST TO THE SAMPLE PROBLEM, HOWEVER, BECAUSE IT IS A CHANGE OF SIGN AND NOT A MARGINAL RATIO: E71 gross = -$20.43 + $81.43 = +$61.00, i.e. +$1.85 per trade. E73 gross = -$311.22 + $57.22 = -$254.00, i.e. -$11.04 per trade. THE WIDER SHIELD TURNED A GROSS-POSITIVE SHORT INTO A GROSS-NEGATIVE ONE. MY HYPOTHESIS WAS WRONG, AND IN AN INSTRUCTIVE WAY. The fee-saving mechanism worked EXACTLY as predicted -- commission per trade was $2.47 at a $1,000 shield and $2.49 at $2,000, flat to two cents, confirming that the fee does not scale with the shield. But the edge did not survive being asked for a bigger move: win rate fell 36.36363636% to 30.43478261%, dropping BELOW the 33.3% that an rr of 2.0 requires, where E71 was above it. A 2R target on a $2,000 shield is a $4,000 move, 4.3%-6.3% of price across this window, against $2,000 (2.2%-3.2%) at E71's setting. THAT IS THE REGISTERED OUTCOME 'GROSS PER TRADE DOUBLES BUT PF DOES NOT CROSS' with a sharper edge than registered: the target became unreachable rather than merely harder. THE CAP IS NOT THE CULPRIT and this was checked before concluding: avgBarsWinning 5839 against a 12,960 cap is 45% of the budget, so HARD LESSON 38's truncation confound does NOT apply and the comparison is clean. WHAT THIS CLOSES: the shield axis is now CLOSED ON THE SHORT as well as the long, and for the OPPOSITE reason to the one I proposed. Fees are real but they are not the lever -- widening the shield to dilute them destroys more edge than it saves. $1,000 sits at or near the useful maximum for this geometry, which makes E71's configuration the good one rather than a starting point. WHAT REMAINS TRUE: E71's short is gross-positive with a win rate above its own break-even, and it is fee-bound in a way that CANNOT be fixed by widening. The remaining honest levers are lower-cost execution or a higher-frequency variant of the same edge, neither of which this harness can express at the forced 0.05%/side parity profile. The 1m window is 4.5 months of ONE regime and cannot support a split; stated, not engineered around.

name: E74: the SHORT without the whole-number band -- first binding test ever run on this leg
description: E71 byte-identical with ONE term removed: the whole-number band, which bans entries when price sits in the x400-x600 middle of a thousand. THE FIRST BINDING TEST EVER RUN ON THE SHORT LEG. All four entry terms were swept on the LONG (E69a h1Bull, E69b the band, E70a brokeBelow, E70b timeGate) but none had ever been tested on the short, for a reason only understood today: at 100% equity the margin call ended almost every short before the shield could act (HARD LESSON 42), so no short measurement meant anything. E71's declared 25%-equity deviation made the leg measurable, and the queue's own hypothesis list named the term to start with -- 'the whole-number band is oriented for longs'.
verdict: THE FIRST PROFITABLE WAR FORMATION SHORT -- but it does NOT KEEP under RATCHET v2 as written. Clause 2 fails.
notes: THE QUEUE'S OWN HYPOTHESIS IS CONFIRMED: THE WHOLE-NUMBER BAND IS ORIENTED FOR LONGS. Against E71 (PF 0.97315988 / DD 2.66826642% / 33 trades / 36.36363636% win / Sharpe -0.11260373 / net -0.20431733%): removing the band gives PF 1.16714444 / DD 3.61455016% / 41 trades / 41.46341463% win / Sharpe 0.77715586 / net +1.48927615%. THIS IS THE FIRST PROFITABLE SHORT IN THE PROJECT'S HISTORY, across every construction in both labs.
